title: Falls and Fall Prevention in Parkinson's
content: People with Parkinson's disease may have an increased risk of falls because of balance problems, freezing of gait, slower movements, posture changes and difficulty turning. Fall risk can also be affected by dizziness, low blood pressure, vision problems and environmental hazards. Practical safety measures may include keeping walking areas clear, improving lighting, using stable footwear and discussing repeated falls with a healthcare professional or physical therapist. Recurrent falls, sudden worsening of balance or injuries from a fall should be medically evaluated. A fall or balance problem alone does not confirm Parkinson's disease.
